G7_grid_convergence.note: worst relative change between the core and fine profiles across band area, weighted area, retarded-window endpoints and mean redshift, over all three orders. Tolerance frozen at 2e-02 from pilot evidence: the pilot measures 1.255e-02, so the threshold leaves roughly a factor of 1.6 of headroom.

G8_cross_tracer.note: worst relative disagreement in equatorial source radius between AART and kgeo at commit dc347060c5fb, over 430 rays stratified by screen azimuth, source radius and delay quantile across all three orders. Tolerance frozen at 1e-09: the pilot measures 1.082e-12, leaving about three orders of magnitude of headroom, which tolerates elliptic-integral and LAPACK variation between builds while still catching a convention or implementation error.

E3_pilot_no_convention_adjustment.note: the two tracers were compared on raw screen coordinates with no sign flip, axis swap, angle offset or unit rescaling applied to either side. Agreement at this level is therefore evidence that the conventions already match, not that they were made to.

E3_pilot_meets_registered_ray_count.note: valid rays per order at the core profile: {0: 15597, 1: 8531, 2: 4179}; registry requires 1536 per order

G8t_retarded_time_validation.note: largest disagreement in a PAIRWISE emission-time difference between AART and kgeo's independent analytic solution, over 25200 pairs from 225 stratified rays, 16875 of them spanning different orders. Differences are compared so that a common time origin cancels; here the measured common offset is -2.274e-13, i.e. the two codes already share an origin. Tolerance frozen at 1e-03 M, far below any temporal structure the source model resolves.

G8t_azimuth_after_rigid_offset.note: AART and kgeo place phi = 0 on different axes. The offset is 1.570796326795 rad, exactly +1 quarter turns to 1.377e-14. A rigid rotation is a convention, as a common time origin is; what is gated is the residual once one global constant is removed.

G8t_azimuth_offset_is_order_independent.note: spread of the fitted azimuth offset across orders: {'0': 1.5707963267948932, '1': 1.570796326794984, '2': 1.5707963267948537}. This is the gate that matters. A single global rotation only relabels the azimuth axis; an order-dependent or screen-dependent one would corrupt every non-axisymmetric source model, and would not be a convention.

G8t_radius_control.note: source radius on the same stratified sample, confirming the coordinate identification used to extract t and phi is correct

G9c_per_order_ray_count.note: n0_valid=15597, n1_valid=8531, n2_valid=4179, minimum_per_order=4179, total_valid=28307. The reported 4179 was the per-order minimum (n=2), not the combined total; every order independently exceeds 1536.
